pages.text: "Only dry grass for me!" Moya the zebra picked out yellow, dry blades beside the waterhole. Fresh green grass had sprouted after the rain. "I'll eat quickly, then race to the rocky hill!"
"I hate green grass! It's bitter!" Moya pushed it aside with a hoof. Mom looked a little worried. Moya crunched another mouthful of dry grass.
The next morning, Moya had no energy. Their legs felt heavy on the way to the rocky hill. "Where did my strength go?" Even their stripes looked dull.
Kiki the meerkat, the lookout, stood on a rock. "Moya, look at the grown-ups! Let's go where they're eating green grass!" Moya raised their head. "Green...?"
Across the waterhole, everything was green. Dewdrops sparkled on the grass. Adult zebras grazed, their black-and-white stripes shining in the sun. "Wow..." Moya stopped to watch.
Kiki whispered, "Green grass hides strength! Eat some, and your stripes shine and your legs race! I've seen it from my rock!" Really? Moya swallowed eagerly.
Moya bravely tried a mouthful. Chew, chew. "Oh! It's sweet and juicy!" It tasted better than expected. Green grass was yummy, too!
How strange! Moya's heavy legs felt light, and their stripes shone black and white. They stretched their neck and whinnied. "Now I can run to the rocky hill!" Kiki hopped up.
That evening, Moya called first. "Mom, green grass first today! One, a mouthful of green! Two, a mouthful of dry! Three, take turns and eat both!" Mom smiled.
Mom gently curled her neck around Moya's. "Your stripes shine when you eat green grass, too!" Green grass helped Moya feel strong. "Green grass is yummy, too!" Off Moya raced with Kiki.
